Docs File search Codelab Using Google Gemini File Search Tool for RAG
The EU benefits handbook goes into a Gemini File Search store with a region tag, and every answer comes back with file citations. Upload returns an operation, and if you query before it is done you get an answer with no grounding and no error, so always poll. The citation offsets count UTF-8 bytes, not Python characters: the euro sign is 3 bytes and u-umlaut is 2, so a marker placed by character index drifts to the right. Think of a ruler marked in millimetres that you read as centimetres. We insert from the right end first, so the offsets on the left do not move. A likely question is "why not RAG Engine here?": File Search works only with the Gemini Developer API key, storage is free and indexing is billed at embedding rates, but it cannot run in the same call as Google Search grounding. Next: step 4 puts a semantic cache in front of these answers, so repeated questions stay inside the 3 s budget.
Lab 10 GlobalCorp people team · step 4 of 4

Cache repeated answers per region and policy version under 100 ms

lab10_cache_latency.py
import statistics, time
from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from redisvl.extensions.cache.llm import SemanticCache
from redisvl.query.filter import Tag
from redisvl.utils.vectorize import GoogleGenAIVectorizer

BUDGET_MS = {"cache_lookup": 100, "llm": 2500, "total": 3000}
BENEFITS = {"EU": "Gym subsidy: 50% of the membership, up to EUR 40 per month.",
            "US": "Gym subsidy: 50% of the membership, up to USD 45 per month."}
POLICY_VERSION = "2026-10"
llm = genai.Client()
cache = SemanticCache(name="globalcorp_faq", redis_url="redis://localhost:6379",
    distance_threshold=0.08, ttl=24 * 3600,                       # stricter than the 0.1 default
    vectorizer=GoogleGenAIVectorizer(model="gemini-embedding-001", task_type="SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY"),
    filterable_fields=[{"name": "region", "type": "tag"}, {"name": "policy_version", "type": "tag"}])

def answer(q: str, region: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    t, timings = time.perf_counter(), {}
    scope = (Tag("region") == region) & (Tag("policy_version") == POLICY_VERSION)
    hit = cache.check(prompt=q, filter_expression=scope, num_results=1)
    timings["cache_lookup"] = (time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000
    if hit:
        timings["total"] = timings["cache_lookup"]
        return hit[0]["response"], timings
    t1 = time.perf_counter()
    resp = llm.models.generate_content(model="gemini-3.8-flash", contents=q,
        config=types.GenerateContentConfig(system_instruction=f"Answer only from:\n{BENEFITS[region]}", temperature=0))
    timings["llm"] = (time.perf_counter() - t1) * 1000
    cache.store(prompt=q, response=resp.text, filters={"region": region, "policy_version": POLICY_VERSION})
    timings["total"] = (time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000
    return resp.text, timings

QUERIES = [("How much is the gym subsidy?", "EU"), ("What does the gym benefit pay?", "EU"),
           ("How much is the gym subsidy?", "US")]
totals = []
for q, region in QUERIES * 3:
    text, tm = answer(q, region)
    over = [k for k, v in tm.items() if v > BUDGET_MS[k]]
    totals.append(tm["total"])
    print(f"{region:4} {tm['total']:7.0f} ms {'HIT ' if 'llm' not in tm else 'MISS'} {text[:45]!r} {over or ''}")
print(f"p50={statistics.median(totals):.0f} ms  p95={statistics.quantiles(totals, n=20)[18]:.0f} ms")

This is the last step of Lab 10: a RedisVL semantic cache in front of Gemini, with a per-stage latency budget of 100 ms for the cache lookup, 2,500 ms for the LLM and 3,000 ms in total. Walk the bands: the cache uses gemini-embedding-001 and a distance threshold of 0.08, stricter than the 0.1 default, in Redis cosine units where lower is stricter; every lookup and every store carries the same region and policy-version tags, so an EU answer can never serve a US employee and bumping POLICY_VERSION retires every old answer at once. The waterfall shows the nine requests in loop order: two misses at about 1.4 s, then seven hits at about 40 ms, so p50 drops to 40 ms while p95 still shows the miss path. Analogy: the cache is a pigeonhole wall where each region and policy version has its own column, and a new handbook version gets a fresh wall. Likely question: "Why not cache personal answers too?" Because the key is the question text, not the person, so a personal answer would leak to the next employee who asks a similar question; also, when you change the embedding model or the filter fields, RedisVL refuses the old index with the schema error shown, so use a new cache name per model. In production, BENEFITS holds the cited File Search answer from step 3. Next: the three quiet failures of managed RAG and their guards.

Managed RAG fails quietly: early queries, partial imports, distances

globalcorp_people/managed_guards.py · fixes for Lab 10 steps 1-3
import sys, time

def wait_indexed(client, op):                 # File Search: never query before indexing ends
    while not op.done:
        time.sleep(5)
        op = client.operations.get(op)
    return op

def cited_span(block, a) -> str:              # FileCitation offsets are BYTES
    raw = block.text.encode("utf-8")
    return raw[(a.start_index or 0):(a.end_index or 0)].decode("utf-8", "ignore")

EXPECTED_FILES = 14
def check_import(imp) -> None:                # partial failures do not raise
    done = imp.imported_rag_files_count + imp.skipped_rag_files_count
    if imp.failed_rag_files_count or done != EXPECTED_FILES:
        sys.exit(f"import incomplete, see {imp.partial_failures_gcs_path}")

def best_first(ctx) -> list:                  # score is a distance: lower is better
    return sorted(ctx.contexts.contexts, key=lambda c: c.score)

1 · Gemini File Search SymptomRight after upload the answer is empty or has no citations. No error. Citations land in the wrong place on "€" or "ü". Or: ValueError: This method is only supported in Gemini Developer API mode, not in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform mode. CauseIndexing is async. start_index counts bytes. File Search is Developer API only. FixPoll the operation. Slice UTF-8 bytes. Use an API-key client; on GCP use RAG Engine. A store is about 3x the input: 400 MB needs ~1.2 GB, over the 1 GB Free tier.
2 · RAG Engine imports Symptom13 of 14 handbook PDFs import and nothing raises. A Google Drive import ends with an empty corpus and no error. CausePartial failures do not raise. The service account has no permission on the Drive folder. FixCheck failed_rag_files_count and imported == expected. Pass import_result_sink. Queue imports: 3 concurrent per region, 10,000 files per request, 60 RPM data-management APIs.
3 · RAG Engine scores SymptomThe worst chunk is shown first. CauseRagContextsContext.score is a distance: lower is more relevant, [0, 2] for cosine. A descending sort inverts the ranking. FixSort ascending. RetrieveContexts allows 600 RPM per project and region, so cache hot queries.
Managed RAG removes the index work, but each of these three failures is silent, so the guards must live in your code. File Search indexes asynchronously: a query sent before the operation is done gets no grounding and no error, citation offsets are bytes so a Python string slice drifts on the euro sign or an umlaut, and the store is Developer API only, so an enterprise client raises the ValueError shown. RAG Engine returns success when 13 of 14 handbook PDFs import, and a Drive import without folder permission imports nothing at all, so count every file you expect and keep a result sink. Its context score is a distance, so lower is better and a descending sort puts the worst chunk on top. Analogy: a courier who leaves the parcel at the wrong door still marks it delivered. Likely question: "Why not just retry the import?" Retry is fine, but only the count tells you that you need one, and the quota allows only 3 concurrent imports per region. Next: three recent papers on latency and composition budgets.
arXiv Aug–Oct 2026 · latency and composition budgets

Budget k per query, and test every change inside the full stack

arXiv 2608.08237 8 Aug 2026

SAGE: SLO-Aware Adaptive Retrieval for Production RAG Systems

A learned per-query k, with no LLM call. Under a 5 s P95 SLO: compliance 95% vs 30% for static k = 20, P95 −36%, retrieval cost −51%, at −2 pts EM. Holds across 4 LLM families.
Top-k is not a fixed budget. 2609.15143 keeps 95–97.7% of nDCG@20 with 66–99.5% fewer accesses.
arXiv 2610.29722 21 Oct 2026 · IBM

Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality (LASAGNA)

450 configurations, 8 benchmarks, 5K to 200K docs. Three retrieval techniques predicted +47% together and delivered +17%. Better retrieval can hurt faithfulness. The 5K winner is not the 200K winner.
Re-run each change in the full stack at production corpus size. Track retrieval and faithfulness apart.
arXiv 2610.18925 13 Oct 2026

CacheSmith: Accurate RAG Serving under Latency SLOs with Adaptive KV Reuse

Adaptive KV reuse raised quality-gated SLO attainment by up to 27.5%. Naive chunk-KV reuse misses cross-chunk attention.
Self-hosted serving: gate KV reuse on quality, not only on latency.
arXiv 2608.08237 arXiv 2609.15143 arXiv 2610.29722 arXiv 2610.18925
Three recent papers turn the GlobalCorp 3-second budget from a wish into an engineering rule. SAGE learns how many chunks each query needs, with no LLM call: under a 5-second P95 SLO it met the target 95 percent of the time against 30 percent for a static k of 20, at a cost of 2 points of exact match, and the Top-K paper shows the same idea for hybrid fusion. LASAGNA from IBM is the warning for the whole course: three techniques that each looked good alone predicted plus 47 percent together but delivered plus 17, and the best design at 5K documents lost at 200K. CacheSmith matters only if you serve your own model: reuse cached KV blocks when quality holds, because naive reuse drops attention across chunks. Analogy: three supplements that each help do not add up to triple health. Likely question: "Can I tune on a 5K sample and ship at 200K?" No; LASAGNA says re-run the full stack at production size. Blog Go Glean vs Claude Cowork (2026-08-26) Blog Waldo (2026-04-28)
Glean is an enterprise search and assistant company, and its August 2026 post compares its agent with Claude Cowork on more than 180 synthetic tasks from its own data; every number here is a vendor claim, so say so. Step 1 and 2: the cost per task fell from 2.98 to 0.58 dollars and tokens from 4.4 million to 1.3 million, and graders preferred Glean 78 percent of the time. Step 3: the reason is routing, because their Pareto study of 37 configurations found no single best model: Claude Opus 5 at high effort scored 67 at 2.96 dollars, GPT-5.6 Luna scored 55 at 8 cents. Step 4: Waldo, a small Nemotron 3 Nano search model, plans the searches and hands the evidence to the frontier model in about 250 milliseconds per call against about 3 seconds. Analogy: a librarian finds the books before the expert reads them. Likely question: "Should GlobalCorp route models?" Measure cost per successful task first, including retries; route only when the labelled set shows that a cheaper model passes. Next: the closing checklist, one rule per lab.
Best practices

Monday checklist: ten rules for shipping RAG in October 2026

  • Run a 100-300 query labelled set and evalkit floor in CI.
  • Parse once, pinned; chunk with the embedder's tokenizer.
  • Content-hash chunk IDs. One index per model + dim.
  • Hybrid + rerank, checked per corpus. Pin RRF k.
  • Score-gate rewrites and loops; budgets in code.
  • Cite raw chunks or byte spans. Summaries score 0.12.
  • Gate releases on recall, canaries, calibrated judge.
  • Filter by groups in the query; nightly injection tests.
  • Budget each stage. Cache only non-personal, policy-scoped answers.
  • Chunk or embedder change = new corpus. Delete test stores.
  • Federate live MCP calls. Up to 45 s vs seconds.
  • Ship a part untested in the full stack. +47% → +17%.

# rag-config.yaml -- every knob that changes ranking, cost or safety, under review
embedding: {model: Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, dim: 256, normalise: true, version: 2026-10}
chunking: {tokenizer: Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, max_tokens: 512, chunker: docling-hybrid}
retrieval: {fusion: rrf, rrf_k: 60, depth: 20, rerank_candidates: 40, keep: 10}
rewrite: {gate_top1_score: 0.55, keep_original_weight: 2.0}
agent: {max_attempts: 3, recursion_limit: 20}
eval_gate: {min_rows: 50,

This is the whole deck as ten rules, and each rule carries the badge of the lab where you built it, so the course map from the opening lights up as we go. Steps 1 to 3 walk the config file in the same order: the offline lane and retrieval, then the loop, citations and the release gate, then security, latency and cache for GlobalCorp. Step 4 adds two don'ts with their evidence: Dropbox measured federated MCP queries at up to 45 seconds, and LASAGNA showed that three tricks predicted to give plus 47 percent together gave only plus 17, plus the managed-versus-self-hosted table. Analogy: the config file is the pre-flight checklist; the pilot does not skip a line because the last flight was fine. Likely question: "Which option do I pick for GlobalCorp?" File Search for the EU benefits handbook because it is cheap and cites bytes, RAG Engine where VPC-SC and CMEK are required, and self-hosted only when you can own the upgrades and CVEs.
